## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `Cache.set` method doesn't lower-case keys, which breaks the case-insensitive key rule documented in this class. Any caller that passes a key with capital letters can't read back what it stored, so this needs fixing before merge. The `DEFAULT_TTL` change and its comment match each other.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — `set` writes `self._store[key]` with the key as given, but the comment at `app/cache.py:14-15` says "every path into _store lower-cases the key first", and `get` (lines 17 and 22) only ever looks up `key.lower()`. As a result, `c.set("Alpha", 1)` followed by `c.get("Alpha")` or `c.get("alpha")` returns `None`. The new round-trip test only calls `set` with the already-lowercase `"alpha"`, so it doesn't catch this. Could you change line 27 to `self._store[key.lower()] = ...` and add a test that calls `set` with a mixed-case key? — Any value stored under a key with capital letters can never be read. Its entry also stays in `_store` forever, because `get` only deletes the lowercase key, so these entries pile up for the life of the cache.

## Strengths
- `test_entries_expire` replaces `time.monotonic` with a controlled clock, so the expiry check doesn't depend on real time passing. The patch works because `app/cache.py` looks up `time.monotonic` through the module at call time.
- The comment on `DEFAULT_TTL` ("300 seconds") matches the new value, and `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes` checks that value.
